working_title: From Identifiability Limits to Mechanism-Resolving Observation Design
editorial_principle: One measurement-design pipeline with two gates: first ask whether an observation can change structural identification; then rank verified candidates by information about the remaining declared mechanism ambiguity.

source_modules.role: structural-identification gate and interpretable field-like measurement witness
source_modules.headline_condition: An added exact scalar log-linear observation reduces unidentified dimension iff its row lies outside the current observation row span.
main_text_use: one pollination-style W=VED witness with two latent mechanisms producing the same current observations
distinction between precision gain and structural identification gain

source_modules.role: admissible-mechanism region, observation information value, sequential design, and frozen controlled validation
source_modules.headline_method: For verified candidate outcome partitions, V(Q)=I(S;Q|A_epsilon)/K ranks current mechanism information; after a selected outcome the admissible region may be conditioned and values recomputed.
source_modules.adaptive_claim_ceiling: The theorem gives V_adapt >= V_static and exact strictness under absence of a common branchwise maximizer, but the frozen G2 benchmark does not provide material empirical evidence that adaptive recomputation beats a static initial-information ranking on those benchmark systems.

dependency_contract.handoff: Boundary is a structural design gate; MROD is a conditional information-allocation method over a declared admissible mechanism region. MROD is not restricted to Boundary's multiplicative/log-linear model.
forbidden_implications: Boundary theorem validates the MROD algorithm
MROD benchmark validates the Boundary ecological factorization
structural non-identifiability means more replication is statistically useless
frozen G2 proves adaptive recomputation is empirically superior to static initial-information ranking
MROD is globally optimal among all sequential experimental-design methods
synthetic validation identifies a natural ecological mechanism

main_text_spine: mechanism ambiguity is a measurement-design problem, not only a model-ranking problem
Gate 1: does a candidate observation change structural identification?
Gate 2: among verified informative candidates, which has the greatest current mechanism information?
conditional theorem for when outcome-dependent recomputation has strict value
frozen controlled benchmark validates information-guided candidate screening against random order
post-frozen diagnostic limits the empirical adaptivity claim

word_budget.note: Boundary calibration transport and extended proof material move to Supporting Information.

development_firewall.promotion_rule: The integrated draft may replace the standalone MROD submission only after its own format, prior-art, source-provenance, and reviewer-bundle checks pass.

priority_firewall: Do not claim novelty for structural identifiability, rank-nullity, mutual information, value of information, approximate Bayesian computation, or adaptive experimental design as generic subjects.
The integrated contribution is the two-gate ecological measurement-design pipeline plus source-owned exact conditions and controlled validation under explicit claim ceilings.
